title: Healing
definition: Healing is God's work of restoring what is wounded, broken, sick, damaged, or sinful according to His wisdom, timing, and purposes.
summary: Healing belongs to God, who restores bodies, hearts, relationships, and ultimately all creation in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus healed the sick, forgave sinners, restored the broken, and will bring complete healing in the new creation.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God is the healer. Scripture shows Him healing bodies, binding wounds, forgiving sin, restoring hearts, and promising final healing in the new creation.

Healing may come in different ways and timing. Sometimes God heals quickly, sometimes gradually, sometimes through means such as care and medicine, and sometimes final healing awaits resurrection.

Christ's healing ministry points to the kingdom of God and the final restoration He will bring. Every present healing is a mercy; complete healing is secured in the hope of resurrection.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People can become discouraged when healing does not come the way they hoped. This doctrine matters because it encourages prayer for healing while anchoring hope in God's wisdom and final restoration.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pray boldly for healing while trusting God's wisdom. Seek appropriate help, receive care, and hold firmly to the promise that Christ will one day make all things new.
